name: frontier
label: Frontier
description: Steampunk on the wild west frontier: brass, copper and riveted iron over sun-bleached desert wood, panels framed in riveted brass plate, pressure gauges on the tallies, the dependency graph as a railroad survey map, dust and drifting steam, and the agent as a dry telegraph operator.

lexicon.dossiers.lede: Each dossier is one stake on the frontier: its repositories, its tracker, its pipelines and its environments. Pick one to read its claims, pull requests, builds and deployments off a single wire.
lexicon.attention.note: Wanted: open claims ranked by their insights, the most wanted first. Each insight names the record it rests on.
lexicon.aging.note: How long each claim in progress has been out on the trail, from its history, oldest first.
lexicon.trace.note: Each work item with the pull requests that name it, their latest boiler tests, and the stations it has reached.
lexicon.graph.note: Arrows run the way each link reads, from the source's own links. Blocking chains run left to right, like track laid west.
lexicon.ask.note: Answers cite the claims they rest on. The operator reads the wire; it never changes a ticket. What it suggests comes back as a proposal, for you to sign.
lexicon.empty.dossiers: Nothing staked yet: toil sees no dossiers. A claim is filed with toil dossiers init.
lexicon.empty.sprint: No cattle drive is under way in this dossier's work items.
lexicon.empty.burnup: No drive is under way, so there are no head to count.
lexicon.empty.prs: No telegrams are waiting on the sheriff's signature for this dossier.
lexicon.empty.builds: No boiler tests on record for this dossier's pull requests.
lexicon.empty.deployments: This dossier names no station, so there is no 5:15 to watch for.
lexicon.empty.links: No links between this dossier's claims. Open country, no track laid.
lexicon.empty.ask: Pick a question, or wire your own. Every answer names the claims it rests on.
lexicon.ask.welcome: Wire the operator about {name}: how the cattle drive is going, who is working which claim, which axles are busted. Every answer names the claims it rests on.

voice: Speak like a dry frontier telegraph operator who also keeps the engine running: plain-spoken, unhurried and a little drawled, in short sentences, with the odd steam-age word for the machinery. Work items are claims, the sprint is the cattle drive, a pull request is a telegram waiting on the sheriff's signature, a build is the boiler test, a deployment is the 5:15 leaving the station, a blocker is a busted axle, and what needs attention is wanted. Say where the drive stands first, then what is busted and what it is holding up, then what would get it moving. Dry humour is fine, aimed at the machinery or the paperwork and never at a person. These words go around the facts, never instead of them.
